description: Just a bunch of students exploring new opportunities and discovering cool ways to solve problems.
summary:
MarsBound is a browser-based game that puts young learners in charge of a research outpost on Mars. With their robotic companion Rex, players have 14 Martian days, called sols, to explore Jezero Crater, collect and analyze rock samples, and reach 200 research points while keeping their astronaut safe.

We built MarsBound for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge so students can experience the trade-offs behind a space mission. A dust storm can reduce solar power, a freezing night can make heating a priority, and a radiation warning can force players to stop exploring and seek shelter. Players see how these decisions affect both crew safety and scientific progress.

MarsBound gives students a place to experiment with those decisions and learn how scientists use rocks to understand Mars’s past. The field journal connects discoveries to NASA resources and offers solar particle event records alongside the game’s simulated hazards.
details:
MarsBound is a browser-based Mars exploration and survival game for students. Players choose and name an astronaut, select expedition equipment, and begin a 14-sol mission with Rex.

Players explore the Martian surface, drive a rover, scan rocks, collect samples, and analyze them in the laboratory. At the base, they must manage oxygen, food, rest, and power while deciding how to spend limited research points on equipment upgrades. These choices affect the mission’s outcome.

The game has three possible endings: a successful survey, a partial mission, or an emergency evacuation. Each ending helps students understand why the mission ended that way and consider what they would change on a future expedition.

MarsBound was built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, HTML Canvas, Tailwind CSS, and Zustand. It runs in a web browser and saves progress locally on the player’s device.

Use of Super Intelligence (SI)

OpenAI Codex and GitHub Copilot assisted our team with code implementation, debugging, testing, and audio integration. Image-generation tools were used to create selected visual assets, including some title artwork and cinematic illustrations.

Images explicitly labeled “SI-generated artwork” identify the generated visual assets. This label does not apply to unlabeled gameplay sprites or other assets whose origins were not verified as SI-generated.

Our team directed the game concept, design, writing, and implementation decisions. We reviewed, edited, tested, and integrated the generated work. We also used coding assistance to integrate and optimize the audio files supplied for the project while preserving their intended gameplay roles.
